title: Tracking Function in SCI
official: Exploring the Trajectory of Physical Function After Discharge in People With Spinal Cord Injury
summary: This study aims to understand how people's physical abilities change during the first year after they leave specialist rehabilitation following a Spinal Cord Injury (SCI). It looks at how well people can move, care for themselves, and function in everyday life once they return to living in the community. We want to investigate whether people improve, stay the same, or experience a decline in their physical function over the first 12 months after in-patient rehabilitation. This information will help identify whether additional support or changes in care are needed after discharge from rehabilitation services. Specifically, we aim to recruit 80 people with SCI to explore physical function at three-time points, before discharge, and at 6 and 12 months post discharge from specialist SCI centres. We will also explore relationships between function, Physical Activity (PA) and individual characteristics.
